No tests are visible for this file.
The default brand name is a placeholder that could be mistaken for real output.

terms.meaning: command-line interface, a tool run by typing commands in a terminal
a plain text data format that other programs can read easily
one category of guidance data, such as styles, colors, or industries
a summary of the design direction for one brand, built from the guideline data

depends_on: core (a sibling module in the same folder, imported by name, not in this packet)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and shared search setup
sections.what: Loads the command-line tools and the shared search code from the same folder. It also brings in the list of valid search domains.
sections.why: Lets this script reuse the search engine next to it instead of repeating that logic.
sections.watch_out: Moving this file without its sibling core module breaks every command.

sections.name: format_results
sections.title: Formatting search hits as text
sections.what: Turns a list of search results into numbered blocks of labeled fields. It prints a short message when there are no results.
sections.why: Makes raw search output easy to read at a terminal.
sections.watch_out: The domain input is accepted but never used, so it has no effect on the text.

sections.name: format_brief
sections.title: Formatting the brand brief for display
sections.what: Prints the brief as sections for industry, design style, colors, typography, and suggested deliverables, using short headers. Long descriptions are cut to 60 characters.
sections.why: Presents the brief as a readable summary instead of raw data.
sections.watch_out: The brand name is read without a fallback, so a brief missing that field will crash the display.

sections.name: main (part 1)
sections.title: Command-line options and search routing
sections.what: Defines the options and then chooses one of three modes: a brand brief, a search across all domains, or a search in one domain. Results are printed as text or JSON.
sections.why: Lets one command cover every search and brief need.
sections.watch_out: In brief mode the search text is treated as the industry, which is easy to misread.

sections.name: main (part 2)
sections.title: Trailing blank line in main
sections.what: Contains only an empty line, with no behavior.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Program start when run directly
sections.what: When this file is run as a program, it starts the main routine. When another file imports it, nothing starts.
sections.why: Standard Python pattern that lets other code reuse the functions here.

summary: Command-line search tool for corporate identity design guidelines that can also print a full brand brief.
purpose: Lets a user or Claude look up design guidance, or get a brand brief, from the terminal.
why: Likely reason: gives one simple command to query the shared guideline data without writing code.
how: Reads the query and options. If a brief is requested, builds and shows it. If all domains are requested, searches each one. Otherwise searches a single domain, picking one automatically if none is given. Prints results as text or JSON.
inputs: Search query text, optional domain, maximum result count, brand name, optional style, and a JSON flag.
outputs: Text or JSON printed to the screen.
risks: In brief mode the query is used as the industry, which is easy to misread. The brand name defaults to a placeholder. No errors are caught, so a failing search stops the command with a raw error.
debug: Confirm the core module sits in the same folder. Try the JSON flag to see the raw data. If results are empty, try a different word or name a domain directly.
